expected_behavior: Within an operator-invoked Clarify workflow, accepted answers should flow back coherently into the active specification and its owning roadmap entry. Reconcile directly affected quality-checklist wording and evidence as needed so accepted clarification does not create a preventable downstream blocker. The user explicitly requests that Clarify be able to propagate its clarifying-question results into both roadmap and spec. An explicit answer authorizing a bounded scope change should support its corresponding artifact reconciliation without forcing separate Roadmap Write and Specify invocations solely to copy that accepted decision.
manual_fallback_status: Separate Roadmap Write and Specify phases were recommended but not invoked for this reconciliation. No workaround or technical repair has been applied; accepted scope is already present in the active spec.
observed_behavior: Feature 019 initially addressed catalog Python prerequisites. During Clarify, the user raised the broader Python installation and utility-availability story. A parent-relayed question offered repository-owned FlowKit tooling with Spec Kit compatibility while excluding external-repository and machine-global changes. The user selected that option. Pass 1 recorded runtime-scope-boundary resolved and continued for specification reconciliation. Pass 2 updated the spec with the accepted broader execution-path, dependency/utility inventory and compatibility requirements, preserving the PyYAML regression and Feature 017 evidence limits. The roadmap remained catalog-only. Core Clarify allowed only checkbox-marker changes, so the obsolete catalog-only checklist criterion was unchecked instead of rewritten; coverage references also remained stale. Independent review found no further product ambiguity but blocked on runtime-scope-roadmap-reconciliation and runtime-scope-checklist-reconciliation. The controller recommended separate Roadmap Write and Specify invocations for companion artifacts rather than completing flow-back in the active clarification. This was a boundary restriction, not a helper crash; the compact run uses generic blocker step-failed while its final assessment states companion-scope-artifacts-require-reconciliation.
safety_response: Preserved accepted scope in the specification, retained historical model/runtime/native-test limitations and protected external/machine-global boundaries. Did not silently edit the roadmap or rewrite checklist prose outside installed command permissions. This kept individual command restrictions intact but left known artifact divergence and made the operator repeat workflow coordination. This observation/export records requested prospective behavior only; it does not change governance or workflow implementation.
suggested_change_target: Review the Clarify workflow, core clarification command checklist-write restriction, controller continuation contract and governing flow-back/roadmap authority as one coordinated change. Add declared bounded reconciliation of accepted human clarification into the selected specification and uniquely owning roadmap entry, including directly affected checklist wording and references. Treat the human scope answer as authorization for that exact semantic change; avoid a second exact-patch approval solely to restate it. Preserve main-task questions and same-child relay, reviewed agent dispatch, validation, nonprogress/iteration limits and original evidence. Reassess the resulting artifact set before reporting completion. Ask only for genuinely new or ambiguous consequential decisions, conflicting ownership or unrelated proposed changes. Do not authorize another feature, arbitrary roadmap cleanup, unrequested implementation, Git integration, publication or acceptance. Regression coverage should exercise this reported scope expansion, specification-only answers needing no roadmap change, ambiguous ownership, unanswered material decisions, stale checklist prose, external-scope exclusions and genuine blocked recovery. The fix belongs to a reviewed follow-up, independent of Feature 019 runtime implementation and related to the earlier redundant-intent-gates feedback.
